## G-8/B-3 · Pin rail and Generate

Frontend + backend. One agent. 70 minutes to freeze — build the beat, not the platform.

OBJECTIVE

Glia can hear you and can show you what Cala cited. It cannot yet make the thing the
product is named for. Generate is the last beat of the demo: the transcript, the
distilled idea and the images you kept become one prompt and one original image.

Two properties matter more than polish. Pins must be a real input — the rail says
"conditioning input" and it has to be true, or the whole pinning interaction is a mood
board pretending to be a control. And the final prompt is a deliverable: whatever goes
to fal is shown to the user verbatim. If we cannot show it, we do not send it.

CONTEXT

Read docs/PARTNERS.md §4 (fal) before writing the client. Read apps/web/src/components/
idea-board.tsx, screens/session-screen.tsx, stores/session.ts, and apps/api/glia/
{config.py,contracts.py,api.py,discovery/cala.py} — match their style exactly.

Known constraint, do not fight it: the board's stickers are inline SVG with no public
URL. fal fetches reference images over the internet, so it cannot use them, and neither
can it reach anything on localhost. Design for that, honestly, per the DEGRADATION
section below.

TASK

1. Pin state moves into the session store. idea-board.tsx currently holds pinnedIds in
   local useState — lift it to `pinned: PinnedRef[]` with togglePin/clearPins.

     PinnedRef { id, title, lane, imageUrl: string | null, sourceUrl: string | null }

   The board passes imageUrl: null for stickers. Lane B's tiles will pass a real URL
   into the identical shape — do not build a second pin path for them.

2. The rail. Fixed to the bottom of the viewport, above the mic composer, full width,
   borderless, same neutral palette. Left: pinned thumbnails ~48px, each with an unpin
   affordance on hover and focus. Label the group `N pins · conditioning input`, not
   "Pinned" — the wording states the causal direction the UI is claiming. Right: a
   single `Generate` button. The rail is absent at zero pins and animates in with the
   existing CSS conventions in index.css (`workspace-enter`/`sticker-enter`); main
   dropped the motion dependency, do not resurrect it.

3. `POST /v1/generate`, body { session_id, transcript, pins: PinnedRef[] }, two steps:

   a. Synthesis. One OpenAI call using the existing OPENAI_SYNTHESIS_MODEL setting.
      Input: the transcript, the current VisualIntent from the distiller, and the pin
      titles. Output: ONE concise image prompt, under 80 words, describing subject,
      mood, style, palette and composition. Constrain it with a Pydantic schema so a
      malformed prompt is a validation error, not a broken generation. Never send the
      raw transcript to fal — the summary is the point.

   b. Generation. Submit to fal with X-Fal-Store-IO: 0.
      - Pins carrying a public https imageUrl → FAL_REFERENCE_MODEL
        (flux-pro/kontext/max/multi) with image_urls, capped at FAL_MAX_REFERENCE_IMAGES.
      - No public URLs → FAL_FALLBACK_MODEL (flux/schnell), text only.
      Use fal's queue endpoint and POLL it. Do NOT build a webhook: it needs a publicly
      reachable callback URL and we are on localhost, so it cannot work today. Cap the
      poll at ~45s, then return a typed timeout.
      fal's concurrency limit is 2 on a new account: allow exactly ONE generation in
      flight per session, and reject a second with a typed "already generating".

   Response carries { image_url, prompt, model, reference_count }. Add FAL_KEY,
   FAL_REFERENCE_MODEL, FAL_FALLBACK_MODEL, FAL_MAX_REFERENCE_IMAGES to config.py —
   they are already in the local .env, so read them, do not redefine defaults that
   contradict it. Honour demo_mode="fixture" with a canned result and no network, as the
   realtime and discovery lanes already do.

4. The result view. The generated image takes the workpane, and the synthesised prompt
   renders verbatim beneath it in small muted type, alongside the model id and the
   reference count. The pin rail stays visible so a second Generate is one click away.
   Button states: idle, generating (disabled, quiet pulse — no spinner), error (one
   line plus a correlation id, still re-clickable).

DEGRADATION — read this rather than inventing something

When no pin has a public imageUrl, the pins still steer: their titles go into the
synthesis as visual steering terms, and the response reports reference_count: 0. Do not
silently drop them, do not fabricate a URL, and do not tell the user the image was
conditioned on references when it was not. The rail label stays honest either way
because the titles genuinely reached the prompt.

CONSTRAINTS

TS strict, no `any`, no non-null `!`. mypy --strict, ruff clean, Pydantic v2 at every
boundary, no bare except. No fal or OpenAI key anywhere near apps/web — both calls are
server-side. Explicit timeouts on every outbound call; do not retry a fal submit (it
costs a generation). uv.lock committed. Do not modify README.md or docs/. Do not add a
dependency beyond what fal needs — plain httpx against the REST queue is enough, no SDK.

ACCEPTANCE

Pin three stickers, hit Generate, and an original image appears in the workpane within
~45s with the exact prompt that produced it printed underneath. A second click while
one is running is refused, not queued. Zero pins hides the rail. Fixture mode returns a
canned result with the network unplugged. Nothing in dist/ contains FAL_KEY or the
OpenAI key — grep and prove it. pnpm lint/typecheck/build and uv run mypy . / ruff
check . all pass.
I'll start by reading the required context before writing anything.

1:# Partner technology reference
2:
3:Six partner technologies. The rules require three. Every entry records exact base URLs, auth headers, identifiers and gotchas, verified against vendor documentation on 29 Aug 2026. Where something is undocumented it says so — **do not guess in the submission writeup.**
4:
5:| | Role in Glia |
6:|---|---|
7:| [OpenAI](#1-openai--live-transcription) | Live transcription of speech; prompt synthesis at Generate |
8:| [Cala](#2-cala--entity-resolution-and-cited-source-discovery) | Resolves what you mean; finds the authoritative sources our references come from |
9:| [Pioneer](#3-pioneer-fastino-labs--visual-attribute-extraction) | GLiNER2 extracts visual attributes from speech; gates Cala spend |
10:| [fal](#4-fal--the-final-image) | Generates the final image, conditioned on pinned references |
11:| [Aikido](#5-aikido--security) | Zen runtime firewall (SSRF matters here), CI gating, safe-chain, live security panel |
12:| [Entire](#6-entire--provenance-for-the-build) | Binds every commit to the agent session behind it |
13:
14:Environment variables are per-section and collected at the end.
15:
16:---
17:
18:## 1. OpenAI — live transcription
19:
20:**Docs moved.** `platform.openai.com/docs/*` now 302s to `developers.openai.com/api/docs/*`.
21:
22:**The model landscape changed in late July 2026.** `gpt-4o-transcribe` and `gpt-4o-mini-transcribe` are now listed under *legacy support*. Any tutorial using `?intent=transcription` plus `gpt-4o-transcribe` and the `OpenAI-Beta: realtime=v1` header is describing the deprecated Beta shape. Ignore it.
23:
24:| | |
25:|---|---|
26:| Realtime WS | `wss://api.openai.com/v1/realtime` |
27:| Ephemeral token | `POST https://api.openai.com/v1/realtime/client_secrets` |
28:| WebRTC SDP exchange | `POST https://api.openai.com/v1/realtime/calls` |
29:| File transcription | `POST https://api.openai.com/v1/audio/transcriptions` |
30:| **Deprecated** | `POST /v1/realtime/transcription_sessions`, `POST /v1/realtime/sessions` |
31:| Env var | `OPENAI_API_KEY` |
32:
33:### Models
34:
35:| Model | Use | Price |
36:|---|---|---|
37:| **`gpt-live-transcribe`** | **Ours.** Low-latency realtime with continuous deltas. Tunable `delay`, plus `prompt`, `keywords`, `languages` hints. No timestamps, no speaker labels, no confidence. | $0.017/min |
38:| `gpt-transcribe` | High accuracy, but in Realtime only emits on **committed turns** — no interim deltas. Default for the file API. | $0.0045/min |
39:| `gpt-realtime-whisper` | **Avoid.** Turn detection must be `null`; VAD is unsupported. | $0.017/min |
40:| `whisper-1` | Legacy; kept for timestamps and translation. | — |
41:
42:Continuous transcription is roughly **$1.02/hour/speaker**. `gpt-live-transcribe` is ~3.8× `gpt-transcribe` — that is the price of deltas, and deltas are the product's feel, so we pay it.
43:
44:### Session type
45:
46:There is a transcription-only mode, but the mechanism changed: open a normal `/v1/realtime` connection and declare `session.type = "transcription"`. Do **not** call the deprecated `/realtime/transcription_sessions` endpoint.
47:
48:### Backend mints the ephemeral token
49:
50:`expires_after.seconds` accepts **10–7200, default 600**. Keep it short.
51:
52:```python
53:from openai import OpenAI
54:client = OpenAI()
55:
56:@app.post("/api/realtime-token")
57:def mint_token():
58:    secret = client.realtime.client_secrets.create(
59:        expires_after={"anchor": "created_at", "seconds": 600},
60:        session={
61:            "type": "transcription",
62:            "audio": {"input": {
63:                "format": {"type": "audio/pcm", "rate": 24000},
64:                "noise_reduction": {"type": "near_field"},
65:                "transcription": {
66:                    "model": "gpt-live-transcribe",
67:                    "languages": ["en", "es"],
68:                    "delay": "low",
69:                    "prompt": "A person thinking out loud about an image they want to create.",
70:                },
71:                "turn_detection": {
72:                    "type": "semantic_vad",
73:                    "eagerness": "low",
74:                },
75:            }},
76:        },
77:    )
78:    return {"value": secret.value, "expires_at": secret.expires_at}
79:```
80:
81:Realtime is now a **top-level** SDK resource — `client.realtime.*`, not `client.beta.realtime.*`. Send `OpenAI-Safety-Identifier: <hashed-user-id>` on the mint call.
82:
83:The `prompt` field is a genuine quality lever for us: telling the model the speaker is describing an imagined image measurably improves how it handles visual vocabulary. The `keywords` field is worth trying with art-movement and style terms.
84:
85:### Browser: WebRTC
86:
87:```js
88:const { value: EPHEMERAL_KEY } = await (await fetch("/api/realtime-token", { method: "POST" })).json();
89:
90:const pc = new RTCPeerConnection();
91:const ms = await navigator.mediaDevices.getUserMedia({ audio: true });
92:pc.addTrack(ms.getTracks()[0]);
93:
94:const dc = pc.createDataChannel("oai-events");   // the name is required
95:
96:dc.addEventListener("message", (e) => {
97:  const ev = JSON.parse(e.data);
98:  switch (ev.type) {
99:    case "conversation.item.input_audio_transcription.delta":
100:      paintInterim(ev.item_id, ev.delta);
101:      break;
102:    case "conversation.item.input_audio_transcription.completed":
103:      sendSettledTurn(ev.item_id, ev.transcript);   // → our WebSocket
104:      break;
105:    case "input_audio_buffer.speech_stopped":
106:      markPause();                                   // → triggers the distiller
107:      break;
108:  }
109:});
110:
111:const offer = await pc.createOffer();
112:await pc.setLocalDescription(offer);
113:const answer = await fetch("https://api.openai.com/v1/realtime/calls", {
114:  method: "POST",
115:  body: offer.sdp,
116:  headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${EPHEMERAL_KEY}`, "Content-Type": "application/sdp" },
117:});
118:await pc.setRemoteDescription({ type: "answer", sdp: await answer.text() });
119:```
120:
121:**Three traps, all verified:**
122:
123:1. **Do not append `?model=` to `/v1/realtime/calls`** — it returns an empty `400`. The model is already baked into the ephemeral secret.
124:2. The docs show **two body shapes** for `/realtime/calls`: the guide's working sample posts raw SDP with `Content-Type: application/sdp`; the API reference describes a form body with `sdp` and `session` parts. Start with raw SDP. Which is canonical is unverified.
125:3. **There is no documented end-to-end WebRTC + transcription-session example.** `client_secrets` explicitly accepts a transcription session, so it is supported on paper, but the combination is unproven in the docs. Since we send audio only, we may need `pc.addTransceiver('audio', { direction: 'sendonly' })` — undocumented.
126:
127:**De-risk this first.** It is the single highest-uncertainty item in the build. If WebRTC resists after 30 minutes, fall back to browser → our FastAPI WebSocket → OpenAI WebSocket, which is fully documented. Cost: one extra hop of latency and our server carries audio bytes.
128:
129:### WebSocket fallback
130:
131:`wss://api.openai.com/v1/realtime`, header `Authorization: Bearer $OPENAI_API_KEY`, no `OpenAI-Beta` header. Audio is **16-bit PCM, 24 kHz, mono, little-endian, base64**, declared as `{"type": "audio/pcm", "rate": 24000}`. Max 15 MB per appended chunk.
132:
133:Client → server: `session.update`, `input_audio_buffer.append` (`{type, audio}`), `input_audio_buffer.commit`, `input_audio_buffer.clear`.
134:
135:Server → client: `conversation.item.input_audio_transcription.delta` (`{type, item_id, content_index, delta}`), `.completed` (`{type, item_id, content_index, transcript}`), `.failed`, `.segment`, `input_audio_buffer.speech_started`, `.speech_stopped`, `.committed`, `.cleared`, `.timeout_triggered`.
136:
137:Reconcile deltas by `item_id` — finals can arrive across turns.
138:
139:### Turn detection — the trigger for our whole loop
140:
141:Set at `session.audio.input.turn_detection`. Three states: `null` (manual commit), `server_vad`, `semantic_vad`.
142:
143:- `server_vad`: `threshold` (0–1, default 0.5), `prefix_padding_ms`, `silence_duration_ms`.
144:- `semantic_vad`: `eagerness` — `low | medium | high | auto` (auto ≡ medium). `low` waits longer before calling end-of-turn.
145:
146:**Use `semantic_vad` with `eagerness: "low"`.** People thinking out loud pause mid-sentence constantly; silence-based VAD would fire the distiller on every breath and shred the transcript into fragments. `create_response` and `interrupt_response` are conversation-mode only and irrelevant to us.
147:
148:Trigger downstream work on `input_audio_buffer.speech_stopped`, then use the `...transcription.completed` for that `item_id` as the settled text.
149:
150:### SDKs
151:
152:Backend: the `openai` Python package, used **only** for `client.realtime.client_secrets.create`. Browser: plain `RTCPeerConnection`, ~30 lines. The agents SDKs (`openai-agents`, `@openai/agents-realtime`) are built for bidirectional voice agents and **do not document transcription-only sessions** — skip them.
153:
154:### Limits
155:
156:`gpt-live-transcribe`: Tier 1 500 RPM / 60,000 TPM, rising to 10,000 RPM / 780,000 TPM at Tier 5. **A concurrent Realtime session cap is not documented** and could not be verified. For long-lived audio streams TPM is the binding constraint — do not plan high concurrency without confirming.
157:
158:### Prompt synthesis at Generate
159:
160:A second, ordinary call — `gpt-5.x` chat completion, or routed through Pioneer — that turns the transcript, the distilled attributes, the pinned reference descriptions and the Cala visual direction into one concise image prompt. This prompt is shown to the user next to the result. It is part of the product, not a hidden internal: *"here is what we understood you to mean."*
161:
162:The event provides claimable OpenAI credits — claim them from the event page before you start.
163:
164:---
165:
166:## 2. Cala — entity resolution and cited-source discovery
167:
168:**Read `docs/STACK.md` § "What Cala actually does here" before writing any code against this API.** Cala returns **no images**. There is no `image`, `image_url`, `thumbnail`, `logo`, `media`, `photo` or `avatar` field anywhere in its OpenAPI schema — verified against `https://api.cala.ai/openapi.json`. It does not crawl the web. Its own docs say so explicitly.
169:
170:| | |
171:|---|---|
172:| Base URL | `https://api.cala.ai/v1` |
173:| Auth header | `X-API-KEY: <key>` — **not** `Authorization: Bearer` |
174:| Env var | `CALA_API_KEY` (our convention; Cala documents none server-side) |
175:| Keys | https://console.cala.ai/api-keys |
176:| SDK | none — raw HTTP. OpenAPI at `https://api.cala.ai/openapi.json` |
177:
178:### Endpoints
179:
180:| Endpoint | Method | Returns |
181:|---|---|---|
182:| `/v1/knowledge/search` | POST | Markdown answer + claim-level citations. **The one that yields scrapeable pages.** |
183:| `/v1/knowledge/query` | POST | Typed JSON rows, **no citations** |
184:| `/v1/entities` | GET | Fuzzy entity name search — our resolution step |
185:| `/v1/entities/{id}` | **POST** | Full entity, properties as `{value, sources[]}` |
186:| `/v1/entities/{id}/introspection` | GET | What fields exist, before you ask |
187:
188:`/v1/entities/{id}` is **POST**, not GET — the body selects properties and relationships.
189:
190:### Step 1 — resolve the spoken subject
191:
192:```bash
193:curl "https://api.cala.ai/v1/entities?name=Bauhaus&limit=10" -H "X-API-KEY: $CALA_API_KEY"
194:```
195:
196:`name` (required), `entity_types` (array), `limit` (1–100, default 20). Returns `{id, name, entity_type, description}`.
197:
198:Entity types are listed inconsistently across docs pages — 16 on the feature page, 31 in the API reference. Confirmed useful for us: `Company, Person, Product, Organization, WorkOfArt, Location, GPE, Country, EducationalInstitution, Facility, Industry, CorporateEvent, Award, Animal`. Do not hardcode the full list from one page.
199:
200:### Step 2 — find cited sources
201:
202:```bash
203:curl -X POST https://api.cala.ai/v1/knowledge/search \
204:  -H "X-API-KEY: $CALA_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
205:  -d '{"input": "Bauhaus design movement visual characteristics"}'
206:```
207:
208:Request: `input` (required), `explainability` (bool, default true), `return_entities` (bool, default true).
209:
210:```jsonc
211:{
212:  "content": "markdown answer",
213:  "explainability": [                       // → salience: which facts carried the answer
214:    { "content": "supporting statement", "references": ["<knowbit-uuid>"] }
215:  ],
216:  "context": [
217:    { "id": "<knowbit-uuid>",
218:      "content": "the quoted evidence",
219:      "origins": [
220:        { "source":   { "name": "Impact Loop", "url": "https://www.impactloop.com/" },
221:          "document": { "name": "Article title",
222:                        "url": "https://www.impactloop.com/artikel/..." },   // ← SCRAPE THIS
223:          "breadcrumb": [""] } } ] },
224:  "entities": [
225:    { "id": "<uuid>", "name": "…", "entity_type": "Company", "mentions": ["…"] } ]
226:}
227:```
228:
229:**`context[].origins[].document.url` is the whole image pipeline.** Documented examples are ordinary article pages on real publications (impactloop.com, seedtable.com, cleantechforeurope.com) — pages that carry `og:image` and inline article images. We fetch those, extract, and badge each resulting candidate with `source.name` and `document.name`.
230:
231:### The trap: entity sources are NOT scrapeable
232:
233:`POST /v1/entities/{id}` property sources use a **completely different `document` shape**:
234:
235:```json
236:{ "name": "GLEIF",
237:  "document": { "endpoint": "https://api.gleif.org/api/v1/lei-records?filter…",
238:                "params": {},
239:                "response_hash": "7089723cc94015908b284e2637d34fca…" },
240:  "date": "2026-02-26" }
241:```
242:
243:Those are raw JSON API endpoints. No `og:image`, nothing to scrape. **Only the `knowledge/search` path yields images.** Two different `document` schemas on two endpoints — write two parsers and do not confuse them.
244:
245:(The `response_hash` is a SHA-256 of the upstream response, which makes entity properties genuinely auditable. Not needed for the image loop, but a nice detail if a judge asks how deep the provenance goes.)
246:
247:### `/v1/knowledge/query` — not for us
248:
249:Returns `{results, entities}` with **no `explainability` and no `context`**, so no citations and no URLs. Row keys are also derived per query rather than a fixed schema. Useful for tabular lookups, useless for image discovery. Cala QL dot-notation (`OpenAI.founded.year`, `startups.location=Spain.funding>10M`) works on both knowledge endpoints, but our inputs come from speech, so we send natural language.
250:
251:### Credits — the budget
252:
253:| Plan | Credits/month | Rate limit |
254:|---|---|---|
255:| Starter (free) | 100 | 10 req/min |
256:| Explore $50 | 1,100 | 100 req/min |
257:| Build $200 | 5,000 | 100 req/min |
258:
259:**1 credit = 1 query, and the binding constraint is the monthly cap, not the rate limit.** Free tier is 100 credits *per month* — roughly three queries a day, which a continuous speech loop exhausts in seconds.
260:
261:**We have 1,100 credits** (100 plan + 1,000 purchased, plan renews 29 Sep 2026). That is comfortable but not infinite: it is roughly 70–200 full demo sessions, or far fewer if the loop leaks. Purchased credits never expire.
262:
263:Budget for today:
264:
265:| | Credits |
266:|---|---|
267:| Development and debugging | ~300 |
268:| Rehearsals | ~100 |
269:| Live demo (×2, including the finalist stage) | ~30 |
270:| Headroom | the rest |
271:
272:Four controls, all mandatory — the budget is comfortable only because they exist:
273:
274:1. **Distiller gate** — no Cala call unless the GLiNER2 attribute set changed materially.
275:2. **Debounce** — 8 s minimum of new settled speech between queries.
276:3. **Cache** — Postgres, keyed on a hash of `input`, raw JSON retained for the source panel. Re-running the demo script must cost zero.
277:4. **Ledger** — Redis counter, surfaced in the dev HUD. A leaking loop is then visible in seconds rather than at 18:00.
278:
279:`429` returns `{"error": "rate_limit_exceeded", …}`; `422` for validation. **Undocumented:** whether `/v1/entities` and introspection consume credits, `Retry-After` headers, `X-RateLimit-*` headers, concurrency limits. Measure entity-call cost against the console meter in the first hour — do not assume lookups are free, and do not discover they are not on credit 900.
280:
281:### Coverage
282:
283:Finance and compliance dominate: SEC/EDGAR, GLEIF, business registries, OFAC/EU/UN sanctions, PEPs, PACER, CourtListener, Fed/ECB/BIS series, Moody's/S&P/Fitch, Reuters, PR Newswire. Healthcare, legal, HR and agro are advertised; only legal has named sources.
284:
285:**Plan for misses.** Most spoken visual thinking is not finance. Cala will often return nothing usable, which is exactly why Lane B is first-class. For the scripted demo, choose a subject inside Cala's coverage so Lane A visibly fires — a company, a product, a place, a named work — and let free-form talk fall through to Lane B.
286:
287:### MCP (dev convenience, not runtime)
288:
289:```json
290:{ "mcpServers": { "Cala": { "url": "https://api.cala.ai/mcp/",
291:                            "headers": { "X-API-KEY": "YOUR_CALA_API_KEY" } } } }
292:```
293:
294:Tools: `knowledge_search`, `knowledge_query`, `entity_search`, `entity_introspection`, `retrieve_entity`. Useful for exploring coverage while building. **Every MCP call spends a credit** — do not leave an agent looping on it.
295:
296:---
297:
298:## 3. Pioneer (Fastino Labs) — visual attribute extraction
299:
300:Pioneer is the **cost gate**. It runs on every speech pause; Cala runs only when Pioneer says the idea actually moved. Encoder models cost $0.15/1M tokens and return in milliseconds, so this is affordable at a cadence that a frontier model never would be.
301:
302:| | |
303:|---|---|
304:| API root | `https://api.pioneer.ai` |
305:| OpenAI-compatible | `https://api.pioneer.ai/v1` → `/chat/completions`, `/completions`, `/responses`, `/models` |
306:| Anthropic-compatible | same base → `/v1/messages` |
307:| Native | `POST https://api.pioneer.ai/inference` |
308:| Auth | `X-API-Key: <key>` or `Authorization: Bearer <key>` |
309:| Env var | `PIONEER_API_KEY` (docs convention; the SDK does **not** read it automatically) |
310:| Keys | `agent.pioneer.ai/api-keys` |
311:
312:### The distiller
313:
314:GLiNER2's `schema.structures` is built for exactly this: pull typed fields out of free text in one pass.
315:
316:```json
317:POST /inference
318:{
319:  "model_id": "fastino/gliner2-multi-v1",
320:  "text": "<the settled transcript window>",
321:  "schema": {
322:    "structures": [{
323:      "name": "visual_direction",
324:      "fields": [
325:        {"name": "subject",     "dtype": "str"},
326:        {"name": "mood",        "dtype": "list"},
327:        {"name": "style",       "dtype": "list"},
328:        {"name": "palette",     "dtype": "list"},
329:        {"name": "composition", "dtype": "str"},
330:        {"name": "medium",      "dtype": "str",
331:         "choices": ["photograph","painting","illustration","3d render","collage","film still"]},

348:
349:Compare the new `visual_direction` against the last one that triggered a Cala query. Spend a credit only when it materially moved:

def extract_subject(transcript: str) -> str | None:
    """A naive noun-phrase heuristic. There is no distiller yet, and this is explicitly the
    placeholder for one: the longest run of capitalised words that is not a sentence opener,
    falling back to the trailing content words.

    a wrong guess is bounded by the debounce and the ledger rather than by the heuristic.

    words = _WORD.findall(transcript)

    best: list[str] = []
    run: list[str] = []
    for index, word in enumerate(words):
        capitalised = word[:1].isupper()

"""Step (b) of Generate: the fal queue, over plain httpx.

Three constraints from docs/PARTNERS.md § 4 shape everything here.

1. Auth is ``Authorization: Key``, **not** ``Bearer``. A 401 is almost always this.
2. ``X-Fal-Store-IO: 0`` on every call. Our prompts contain summarised user speech and there is
   no reason for fal to keep it for thirty days.
3. The throttle is concurrency, and a new account gets two. One generation per session is in
   flight at a time and the second is refused, not queued.

Submit is **never retried**. A duplicate submit is a second billed generation for one click,
and a 202 we failed to read is still a generation running upstream.

Webhooks are deliberately absent. ``?fal_webhook=`` needs a publicly reachable callback and we
are on localhost, so it cannot work today; the queue is polled instead, on a hard cap.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import ipaddress
import time
from typing import Any, Final
from urllib.parse import urlparse

import httpx
import structlog

from glia.config import Settings
from glia.contracts import PinnedRef

logger = structlog.get_logger(__name__)

_TERMINAL_FAILURES: Final = frozenset({"ERROR", "FAILED", "CANCELLED"})


class FalNotConfigured(Exception):
    """No FAL_KEY. The route says so rather than pretending to have generated."""


class FalTimedOut(Exception):
    """The poll cap elapsed. The generation may still complete upstream, and is still billed."""


class FalUpstreamError(Exception):
    """Anything else. The vendor body never leaves this module."""


def is_public_https(url: str | None) -> bool:
    """Whether fal could actually fetch this.

    fal pulls reference images over the internet, so anything that is not public https is not a
    reference: no data: URIs, no blob:, no localhost, no private ranges. A URL that fails this
    is not passed off as a reference and not silently repaired — the pin still steers the
    prompt through its title, and `reference_count` reports the truth.
    """
    if not url:
        return False
    parsed = urlparse(url)
    if parsed.scheme != "https" or not parsed.hostname:
        return False
    host = parsed.hostname.lower()
    if host in {"localhost", "127.0.0.1", "::1"} or host.endswith((".local", ".localhost")):
        return False
    try:
        address = ipaddress.ip_address(host)
    except ValueError:
        return True
    return not (address.is_private or address.is_loopback or address.is_link_local)


def reference_urls(pins: list[PinnedRef], limit: int) -> list[str]:
    """The pins fal can genuinely condition on, capped at FAL_MAX_REFERENCE_IMAGES."""
    return [pin.image_url for pin in pins if is_public_https(pin.image_url)][:limit]


class FalClient:
    """Owns the key, the timeouts, the poll cap and the one-in-flight rule."""

    def __init__(self, settings: Settings) -> None:
        self._settings = settings
        self._queue_base = settings.fal_queue_base_url.rstrip("/")
        self._timeout = httpx.Timeout(
            connect=settings.fal_connect_timeout_seconds,
            read=settings.fal_request_timeout_seconds,
            write=settings.fal_connect_timeout_seconds,
            pool=settings.fal_connect_timeout_seconds,
        )
        self._in_flight: set[str] = set()

    @property
    def configured(self) -> bool:
        return self._settings.fal_key is not None

    def acquire(self, session_id: str) -> bool:
        """Claim this session's single generation slot. False means one is already running.

        A plain set is enough: the event loop never interleaves between this check and the add,
        so two clicks in the same tick cannot both win.
        """
        if session_id in self._in_flight:
            return False
        self._in_flight.add(session_id)
        return True

        self._in_flight.discard(session_id)

            raise FalNotConfigured("FAL_KEY is not set.")

            "Authorization": f"Key {key.get_secret_value()}",

            "X-Fal-Store-IO": "0",

            response_url = self._queue_url(submitted, "response_url")

                model=model,
                reference_count=len(references),
                request_id=submitted.get("request_id"),

        self,
        client: httpx.AsyncClient,
        model: str,
        arguments: dict[str, Any],
        headers: dict[str, str],
    ) -> dict[str, Any]:

            response = await client.post(url, json=arguments, headers=headers)
        except httpx.HTTPError as error:
            # Not retried even when it provably never landed: a submit we cannot account for is
            # cheaper to fail than to risk billing twice for one click.
            raise FalUpstreamError("fal did not accept the request.") from error
        payload = self._json(response, endpoint="submit")
        if not isinstance(payload, dict):
            raise FalUpstreamError("fal returned a non-object submit response.")
        return payload

    async def _await_completion(
        self,
        client: httpx.AsyncClient,
        status_url: str,
        headers: dict[str, str],
        deadline: float,
    ) -> None:
        interval = self._settings.fal_poll_interval_seconds
        while True:
            payload = await self._get(client, status_url, headers)
            status = payload.get("status")
            if status == "COMPLETED":
                return
            if isinstance(status, str) and status.upper() in _TERMINAL_FAILURES:
                logger.warning("fal.request.failed", status=status)
                raise FalUpstreamError(f"fal reported {status}.")
            if time.monotonic() + interval >= deadline:
                logger.warning("fal.poll.timed_out", last_status=status)
                raise FalTimedOut("fal did not finish inside the poll window.")
            await asyncio.sleep(interval)

    async def _get(
        self, client: httpx.AsyncClient, url: str, headers: dict[str, str]
    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
        try:
            response = await client.get(url, headers=headers)
        except httpx.HTTPError as error:
            raise FalUpstreamError("fal did not answer.") from error
        payload = self._json(response, endpoint="poll")
        if not isinstance(payload, dict):
            raise FalUpstreamError("fal returned a non-object response.")
        return payload

    def _json(self, response: httpx.Response, *, endpoint: str) -> Any:
        if response.status_code >= 400:
            # Logged by status, never returned: it is a vendor body and may carry account
            # detail that has no business in an HTTP reply of ours.
            logger.warning("fal.request.rejected", status=response.status_code, endpoint=endpoint)
            raise FalUpstreamError(f"fal returned {response.status_code}.")
        try:
            return response.json()
        except ValueError as error:
            raise FalUpstreamError("fal returned a body that is not JSON.") from error

        """Follow fal's own `status_url` / `response_url` rather than building them.

        The queue paths for a nested model id (`fal-ai/flux-pro/kontext/max/multi`) are not the
        model id — they truncate to the app. Trusting the submit response removes that trap,
        and pinning the host is what keeps a trusted response from becoming an open fetch.
        """
        value = submitted.get(field)
        if not isinstance(value, str) or not value:
            raise FalUpstreamError(f"fal did not return a {field}.")
        parsed = urlparse(value)
        expected = urlparse(self._queue_base)
        if parsed.scheme != "https" or parsed.hostname != expected.hostname:
            raise FalUpstreamError(f"fal returned an unexpected {field}.")
        return value

    images = payload.get("images")
    if isinstance(images, list):

                return str(item["url"])
    single = payload.get("image")
    if isinstance(single, dict) and isinstance(single.get("url"), str):

Done. Generate is wired end to end and verified in the browser.

## What landed

**Pin state lifted into the session store** — [session.ts](apps/web/src/stores/session.ts) now owns `pinned: PinnedRef[]` with `togglePin`/`clearPins`. [idea-board.tsx](apps/web/src/components/idea-board.tsx) pins through it with `imageUrl: null`; Lane B tiles will pass a real URL into the identical shape, no second path.

**The rail** — [pin-rail.tsx](apps/web/src/components/pin-rail.tsx), fixed above the docked mic, full width, borderless, labelled `N pins · conditioning input`. Absent at zero pins, animates in on `workspace-enter`/`sticker-enter`, no motion dependency. A borderless gradient scrim keeps it from colliding with the transcript's last lines.

**`POST /v1/generate`** — [synthesis.py](apps/api/glia/generation/synthesis.py) (one OpenAI call, `json_schema` out, `SynthesisedPrompt` Pydantic in — a malformed prompt is a refusal, never a truncation) then [fal.py](apps/api/glia/generation/fal.py) (queue submit + poll, `X-Fal-Store-IO: 0`, `Authorization: Key`, no submit retry, 45s cap → typed `timeout`, one generation in flight per session → typed `already_generating`). It follows fal's own `status_url`/`response_url` with the host pinned, which sidesteps the nested-model-id queue-path trap and keeps a trusted response from becoming an open fetch. No SDK, no webhook, no new dependency; `uv.lock` unchanged.

**Degradation, as specified** — every pin's title goes into the synthesis; only public-https pins go to fal as `image_urls`. The visible proof: with three stickers pinned the prompt ended `…echoing cobalt observatory, brutalist sun study, quiet mediterranean` and reported `0 reference images`; unpinning one dropped that phrase from the next prompt.

## Verified

Fixture mode, three pins → Generate → image took the workpane with the exact prompt underneath, model id and reference count. Unpin → label went to `2 pins`, regenerate, prompt changed. Zero pins → rail gone. `pnpm lint/typecheck/build`, `uv run ruff check .`, `uv run mypy .`, 58 pytest tests all pass. No key material or server-only endpoint in `dist/` (grepped the literal `.env` values, the variable names, and `queue.fal.run`).

## Two things you should know

**I could not exercise the live fal path.** `FAL_KEY` is empty in the local `.env`, so the network half is verified against a mocked httpx transport only — submit shape, headers, `image_urls`, the reference/fallback model split, the poll timeout, the single-flight refusal, and no-retry-on-submit each have a test. The first real key will be the first real submit. Fixture mode is genuinely offline: its image is an inline SVG data URI, and a test asserts the route opens no connection.

**Generate is only reachable with at least one pin,** since the rail is its only home and the rail is absent at zero. That follows the spec as written, but it means a pinless session can't generate — say the word if you want a fallback entry point.

Two unrelated frictions I hit and did not touch: discovery outranks the board, so once Cala answers the stickers vanish and there is nothing left to pin (I turned live discovery off to test); and the in-app browser blocks microphone access, so I drove the session with a synthetic audio stream rather than a real mic.

Done. The rail is now a bottom banner and, since `FAL_KEY` appeared mid-session, I used it to close the live gap — which turned up two real problems.

## The layout change

The rail is fixed to the floor of the viewport, full width, on its own white ground with a hairline top edge so it reads as one contained thing. The mic composer now docks *above* it, and nothing is overlapped: one `--rail-space` variable reserves the strip in the workspace grid, the transcript's padding and the mic's dock offset, and `:has(.pin-rail)` applies it only while there is a rail. Each tile carries a black X badge on its corner — always visible, not on hover — and the tiles scroll sideways rather than wrapping so the banner's height stays a constant the layout can reserve. Verified at desktop and mobile: pin, unpin from the banner, regenerate, zero pins hides it.

## Two things live fal exposed

**fal cannot fetch `upload.wikimedia.org`.** It answers a blank User-Agent — which is what fal's fetcher sends — with `403`, so fal returns `file_download_error`. This matters beyond today: `docs/PARTNERS.md` names Wikimedia Commons as a primary Lane B source, and those URLs will not work as reference images. Lane B will need a re-host (fal's own `upload_file`) or a different source.

**My client mishandled that, and the fix is a real improvement.** fal marks such a request `COMPLETED` on the status endpoint and only rejects it with a `422` from the *result* endpoint. My code logged both endpoints identically and collapsed the failure into "temporarily unavailable" — misleading, because retrying can never help. There is now a typed `reference_unavailable` status carrying the prompt and reference count, and the rail says *"One pinned image could not be fetched for conditioning — unpin it to generate without it."* That is the one generation failure the user can actually act on. Three tests pin the behaviour, including that an ordinary 422 stays a generic upstream error.

## Live-verified against real fal

Text-only via `flux/schnell` (13.8s). Reference-conditioned via `flux-pro/kontext/max/multi` with `image_urls` (21.8s) — the conditioning path works, which was the single most important unproven claim. The typed reference failure. And two concurrent clicks on one session: first `ok`, second `already_generating`. That cost about six generations on your prepaid balance.

branch and worktree so junk doesn't pile up and eat disk.

- **Consolidate** (push → PR → squash-merge → pull develop): additive only,
  never destroys anything. Run directly, no confirmation.
- **Clean up** (delete branch, remove worktree): the only irreversible part.
  Governed by a hard safety gate — NEVER delete anything whose content is not
  already provably inside `develop`. The gate protects against losing code; it
  is an automatic check, not a "do you want to?" prompt.

The overriding rule: **do not delete code that isn't consolidated.** If any work
is not yet in `develop`, STOP, report exactly what's unconsolidated, and delete

  feature branch INTO develop; it must not run from the base branch.
- **Uncommitted or untracked changes exist** → this is unconsolidated work. Do
  NOT proceed to any deletion. Commit it (sensible message) so it becomes part

- **0 commits ahead of base** → nothing to ship. Tell the user and STOP (don't
  create an empty PR, don't delete anything).

# --delete-branch never runs: the merge lands server-side but the remote branch

  and matches the user's request — do not wait for CI, do not block on it.
- `--delete-branch` deletes the REMOTE branch as part of the merge.
- If `--admin` is rejected (insufficient permissions), report exactly that and
  stop — do NOT silently retry without admin or force-push over branch

### 3. Pull develop
```
git checkout <base>
git pull origin <base>
```
This brings the squashed commit into your local base branch.

## CLEANUP SAFETY GATE (read before steps 4–5)
From here on you delete things. Apply this gate to EVERY delete. Deletion is
allowed ONLY when the target's own work is provably already in `origin/<base>`.

Why the naive checks are wrong:
- `git branch --merged` uses SHA reachability → after a squash-merge the branch's
  commits aren't reachable from develop, so it falsely reports "not merged".
- `git diff <branch> origin/<base>` compares full trees → if develop advanced for
  ANY other reason (another branch merged, someone else's commit), the trees
  differ even though THIS branch's work is fully consolidated. False positive.
- `git diff` WITHOUT `--binary` cannot represent a binary file: it emits the
  placeholder `Binary files a/path and b/path differ`, which `git apply` refuses
  with `cannot apply binary patch to '<path>' without full index line`. Any repo
  that commits a built artifact then fails the gate on EVERY run, even when the
  branch is fully merged. Always pass `--binary`.

Correct, portable check (works on git ≥2.20, no merge-tree needed) — ask only
"are THIS branch's net changes already present in develop?", ignoring whatever
else moved develop. Take the branch's diff since its merge-base and test whether
it REVERSE-applies cleanly to the current develop working tree; if it does,
develop already contains those changes.

A green from this gate authorises `git worktree remove` and `git branch -D`.
That makes it the one gate in this skill whose FALSE POSITIVE destroys work.
Treat it accordingly: the command must name the place it runs, and it must be
proven able to go red in the same run.

The failure this replaces: `git apply --reverse --check` resolves paths against
the CURRENT directory. Run from the worktree — still on the branch — it
reverse-applies the branch's own patch to the branch's own tree, which always
succeeds. Vacuous green. Telling the agent in prose to "run it from develop" is
not enough; put the location inside the command.

Precondition: step 3 already left the MAIN checkout on an up-to-date `<base>`
with a clean working tree. The gate validates that itself and refuses to answer
otherwise — a gate that runs in the wrong place is worse than no gate:
```
MAIN=$(git worktree list --porcelain | head -1 | cut -d' ' -f2)   # first entry is always the main checkout
BASE=$(git merge-base origin/<base> <current-branch>)

if [ "$(git -C "$MAIN" rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD)" != "<base>" ]; then
  echo "GATE_INVALID: main checkout is not on <base>"
elif [ -n "$(git -C "$MAIN" status --porcelain)" ]; then
  echo "GATE_INVALID: main checkout is dirty"
elif [ "$(git -C "$MAIN" rev-parse HEAD)" != "$(git -C "$MAIN" rev-parse origin/<base>)" ]; then
  echo "GATE_INVALID: main checkout is behind origin/<base>"
else
  git diff --binary "$BASE" <current-branch> > /tmp/ship-it-consolidation.patch
  if [ ! -s /tmp/ship-it-consolidation.patch ]; then
    echo CONSOLIDATED          # branch made no net change
  elif git -C "$MAIN" apply --reverse --check /tmp/ship-it-consolidation.patch 2>/dev/null; then
    echo CONSOLIDATED          # develop already contains every net change
  else
    echo NOT_CONSOLIDATED
  fi
fi
```
There are THREE outcomes, not two: consolidated, not consolidated, and NOT
MEASURED. `GATE_INVALID` is the third. It is a STOP, never an override, and
collapsing it into either of the other two is exactly how a vacuous green ships.

### Prove the gate can go red — same run, every run (mandatory)

Before trusting a CONSOLIDATED, confirm the gate is capable of saying the other
thing. The control MUST be git-generated. A hand-written patch is rejected with
`corrupt patch at line N` — a rejection of FORM, not of content. It proves the
patch parser works and says nothing about whether the gate detects absent
changes. A control that cannot fail for the reason you care about is not a
control. A control run once when this skill was written says nothing about the
run happening now, in a different directory.
```
f=$(git diff --name-only "$BASE" <current-branch> | head -1)
git -C "$MAIN" show "origin/<base>:$f" > /tmp/ctl.orig 2>/dev/null || : > /tmp/ctl.orig
{ echo "ship-it negative control marker"; cat /tmp/ctl.orig; } > /tmp/ctl.new
git diff --no-index --binary /tmp/ctl.orig /tmp/ctl.new \
  | sed "s#/tmp/ctl.orig#a/$f#; s#/tmp/ctl.new#b/$f#" > /tmp/ship-it-control.patch
if git -C "$MAIN" apply --reverse --check /tmp/ship-it-control.patch 2>/dev/null; then
  echo "CONTROL_FAILED: the gate greens a change that is absent from <base>"
else
  echo "CONTROL_OK: the gate can go red"
fi
```
Anything other than `CONTROL_OK` means the gate carries no information in this
run. STOP. Remove nothing, delete no branch, and say in the report that the
consolidation verdict was unproven.
`--binary` is load-bearing, not cosmetic: without it the gate is structurally
unable to describe a binary file and reports NOT_CONSOLIDATED for reasons that
have nothing to do with whether the work shipped.

Corroborating per-path blob check (run it whenever the patch gate says
NOT_CONSOLIDATED, and any time the branch touches binaries). It compares content
hashes directly, so it handles binaries head-on and does not depend on patch
application at all — a path that prints nothing is byte-identical in develop:
```
git diff --name-only -z "$BASE" <current-branch> | while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do
  a=$(git rev-parse --quiet --verify "<current-branch>:$f" 2>/dev/null || echo MISSING)
  b=$(git rev-parse --quiet --verify "origin/<base>:$f" 2>/dev/null || echo MISSING)
  [ "$a" = "$b" ] || echo "DIFFERS $f"
done
```
(Use the `-z` / `read -d ''` form rather than `for f in $(git diff --name-only)`:
unquoted word-splitting shatters a path containing a space into phantom entries
that all report DIFFERS. `MISSING` on both sides means the branch deleted the
path and develop did too — consolidated.)

Interpretation:
- **CONSOLIDATED** (empty patch, or reverse-applies cleanly) → every net change
  the branch made is already in develop → safe to delete branch and worktree.
- **NOT_CONSOLIDATED** → DIAGNOSE IT BEFORE YOU TRUST IT OR OVERRIDE IT. Read
  `git apply`'s stderr (re-run without `2>/dev/null`): a genuine miss reports
  `patch does not apply` against text hunks, whereas the binary-representation
  bug above names a binary path and a missing index line. The two look identical
  if you only read the verdict. Corroborate with the blob check, then:
  - Blob check prints nothing → the branch's content IS in develop; the verdict
    was an artifact of the check, not unconsolidated work.
  - Blob check prints `DIFFERS` → treat as real. STOP. Show what's missing with
    `git log --oneline origin/<base>..<current-branch>` and
    `git diff origin/<base>...<current-branch>`, report clearly, and delete
    NOTHING — neither branch nor worktree. Not losing this work is the point.

If the two checks disagree, or you cannot explain the failure, **delete nothing**.
The default when a gate fails is always to preserve; diagnosing is how you earn a
CONSOLIDATED verdict, never a reason to skip the gate or force a deletion.

One residual case both checks share: if develop MODIFIED a file after the merge
that this branch also touched, both report NOT_CONSOLIDATED / DIFFERS even though
the branch shipped. For text the reverse-apply usually still succeeds on context,
but a binary is matched whole-blob, so a rebuilt artifact on develop will trip it.
That is the safe direction — the checks can withhold a deletion they could have
allowed, but they will not call unconsolidated work consolidated. Confirm such a
case by hand (e.g. the squash commit in `git log origin/<base> -- <path>`) before
concluding anything.

This is immune to a develop that moved underneath you, because it inspects only
the branch's own diff, never the full tree.

### 4. Delete the local branch (only if the gate passed)
```
git branch -D <current-branch>
```
`-D` is used because after a squash-merge git's own `-d` merged-check would
refuse — but we've already proven consolidation by content above, so this is
safe. If the content gate did NOT pass, do not run this.

### 5. Worktree cleanup (only if the gate passed)
Worktrees in this repo live under `.claude/worktrees/`. Clean up the worktree
that hosted the merged branch so it stops taking disk. But re-apply the gate per
worktree — a worktree may hold work that never made it into develop.
```
git worktree list
```
For the worktree tied to the merged branch, verify BOTH:
- Working tree clean: `git -C <worktree-path> status --porcelain` is empty
  (no uncommitted/untracked files).
- Commits consolidated: apply the same reverse-apply check to the worktree's
  HEAD, so a moved develop doesn't cause a false block:
  ```
  WT_BASE=$(git -C <worktree-path> merge-base origin/<base> HEAD)
  git -C <worktree-path> diff --binary "$WT_BASE" HEAD > /tmp/ship-it-wt.patch
  # test against up-to-date develop (main checkout is on <base> from step 3)
  if [ ! -s /tmp/ship-it-wt.patch ] || \
     git -C "$MAIN" apply --reverse --check /tmp/ship-it-wt.patch 2>/dev/null; then
    echo WT_CONSOLIDATED
  else
    echo WT_NOT_CONSOLIDATED
  fi
  ```
  `git -C "$MAIN"` is load-bearing here, exactly like `--binary`. Run the apply
  from the worktree and you are testing the branch against itself: it always
  says WT_CONSOLIDATED, and on the other side of that green is
  `git worktree remove`. `$MAIN` comes from the branch gate above, where it was
  validated; if that gate did not run in this same shell, re-derive and
  re-validate it before using it here.
  `--binary` here for the same reason as the branch gate — without it a committed
  binary artifact makes every worktree read WT_NOT_CONSOLIDATED. On
  WT_NOT_CONSOLIDATED, diagnose before trusting it: read `git apply`'s stderr and
  corroborate with the same per-path blob check, substituting the worktree's HEAD:
  ```
  git -C <worktree-path> diff --name-only -z "$WT_BASE" HEAD | while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do
    a=$(git -C <worktree-path> rev-parse --quiet --verify "HEAD:$f" 2>/dev/null || echo MISSING)
    b=$(git rev-parse --quiet --verify "origin/<base>:$f" 2>/dev/null || echo MISSING)
    [ "$a" = "$b" ] || echo "DIFFERS $f"
  done
  ```

Then:
- **Both pass** (clean tree AND WT_CONSOLIDATED) → the worktree holds nothing that
  isn't in develop. Remove it:
  ```
  git worktree remove <worktree-path>
  ```
- **Either fails** → treat it as unconsolidated work (dirty/untracked files, or
  commits not in develop). STOP. List exactly what's uncommitted/undelivered and
  remove NOTHING. Never `--force` a worktree removal that would discard work.
  A WT_NOT_CONSOLIDATED that the blob check contradicts (no `DIFFERS` lines) is
  the check misreading, not surviving work — say so explicitly in the report and
  only then treat the worktree as removable. A dirty working tree is never
  overridable this way: uncommitted files are unconsolidated by definition.

Finally, prune stale bookkeeping for worktrees whose dirs are already gone
(safe — only removes metadata, never live files):
```
git worktree prune -v
```

## Two properties this is built around

**Pins are a real input.** The rail says `conditioning input`, and the backend keeps that claim. Every pin's title goes into the prompt synthesis; every pin carrying a public https URL additionally goes to fal as `image_urls` against `flux-pro/kontext/max/multi`. **The prompt is a deliverable.** Whatever goes to fal is shown to the user verbatim beneath the image. It is constrained rather than trusted — JSON schema out, a Pydantic model with a hard 80-word cap back — so a malformed prompt is a validation error, not a silent truncation. If we cannot show it, we do not send it.

## Backend

`POST /v1/generate` → one OpenAI synthesis (`OPENAI_SYNTHESIS_MODEL`), then fal over plain httpx against the REST queue. No SDK, no new dependency, `uv.lock` unchanged.
